packs.title: Forest, Village & Shore
packs.promise: Find carved wildlife, follow a river and turn south-shore details into small creations.

q.s: Find wildlife in wood at the village.
st: Find the city-listed Wildlife Chainsaw Sculpture in Heavenly Village.
Choose three visible carved details: an animal outline, a tool-mark texture and a change between light and shadow.
Give the three details a six-word title of your own.

q.s: Make an original frame around a public artwork.
st: Locate Washoe Woman using the city art map. Observe the sculpture and read its identification if available.
Frame the work with sky and one nearby texture. Make a small sketch or four-line response about what you can see.
Give your response an original title. Describe your viewpoint without inventing a story or speaking for the Washoe people.

q.s: Turn an exterior detail into a fictional postcard.
st: Use an open estate path to choose one building exterior detail: roof, porch, window or timber.
Sketch a postcard frame containing that detail and one natural feature.
Write two sentences to an imaginary future visitor about what you observed today. Keep invented story separate from history.

packs.title: Al Tahoe & Bijou
packs.promise: Explore neighborhood art, small histories and lake views in two connected afternoons.

q.s: Build a tiny route through Tahoe history.
st: Visit during an open public session. Choose three displayed objects connected with travel, work or a changing Tahoe life.
For each, read the available label and note a visible feature plus one fact the museum actually gives.
Arrange your three objects into a short journey through the museum. Mark your own connections as interpretation.

q.s: Borrow colors and make your own composition.
st: Find three colors in works actually visible in the gallery windows.
After looking, make an original small abstract arrangement with those colors, or write a three-line color score.
Give it a title drawn from today’s light. Keep the composition yours rather than copying an exhibited work.

q.s: Let the lake set the pace for a moment.
st: Choose a dry public stopping place with a lake view away from through traffic.
For one minute notice a near texture, the water’s surface and the far mountain line. Keep eyes open.
Write one word for each distance, then arrange them into a three-word title.
